questions.question_en: Which of the following are NOT necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President's rule in a State? 1. Dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly; 2. Removal of the Council of Ministers in the State; 3. Dissolution of the local bodies
questions.topic: President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.language_status: English structured extraction; Telugu not included in index
questions.explanation_en: When President's Rule is proclaimed: the State Legislature is suspended/dissolved (or kept under suspended animation), and the Council of Ministers is removed. Local bodies (municipalities, panchayats) are NOT necessarily dissolved. So 1 (dissolution may not be immediate) and 3 (local bodies not affected) are not necessary consequences.

questions.question_en: The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the legislative assemblies of States. In this context, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The value of vote of each MLA is determined by dividing the population of the State by the total number of elected members in its legislative assembly and dividing the quotient by 1000. 2. The value of vote of each MP (Member of Parliament) is determined by dividing the total value of votes of all State Assemblies by the total number of elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
questions.language_status: English structured extraction; Telugu not included in index
questions.explanation_en: Statement 1 is incorrect — the MLA vote value formula uses the 1971 census population figure. Statement 2 is correct — MP vote value = total value of all MLA votes divided by total elected MPs.

questions.question_en: Consider the following statements in respect of election to the President of India: 1. Higher the number of elective Assembly seats, higher is the value of vote of each MLA of that State. 2. The value of vote of each MLA of Madhya Pradesh is greater than that of Kerala. 3. The members nominated to either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assemblies of States are also eligible to be included in the Electoral College. 4. The value of vote of each MLA of Puducherry is higher than that of Arunachal Pradesh because the ratio of total population to total number of elective seats in Puducherry is greater as compared to Arunachal Pradesh. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.language_status: English structured extraction; Telugu not included in index
questions.explanation_en: Only statement 4 may be correct about MLA vote value formula. Statement 1 is incorrect (more seats actually means lower value per MLA). Statement 3 is incorrect (nominated members are not in Electoral College). Statement 2 needs verification.
